passage:
Jomon, you cry like the monsoon, don't you? So did I. I'm Vasudha teacher to you now, but at your age I was the loudest girl in our village. When my best friend moved away, I sobbed for three days. When boys teased my frizzy hair, I shouted till the whole lane heard, then hid in the cowshed till dark.
My mother never told me to stop feeling. She would sit by me and ask, 'Is it angry or is it sad? Tell me which.' Just naming it made it smaller. Then she'd send me to splash water on my face at the well and count the steps back.
I still feel everything big, Jomon. Maybe that's why I became a teacher. But now I know how to cool it down.

qa.q: How long did Vasudha sob when her best friend moved away?
qa.a: For three days.

qa.q: Why did Vasudha's mother ask 'Is it angry or is it sad?'
qa.a: She wanted to help Vasudha put a name to the feeling, because naming it made it smaller.

qa.q: What turning point helped young Vasudha handle big feelings?
qa.a: Her mother sitting beside her, asking her to name the feeling and then sending her to splash water at the well and count steps, turned outbursts into something she could manage.

qa.q: How might Vasudha's mother have seen her daughter's outbursts?
qa.a: She seems to have seen them as big feelings to name and cool down, not as bad behaviour to stop.

grounding: Shows, through an elder's memory, a child who loved fiercely and had long, loud upsets, and how naming feelings and cooling down helped.

passage:
The school sports day was cancelled because of rain, and the hall was packed and echoing. Eshaan had waited all week to run the relay with Chaitanya. Now some older boys laughed at his dinosaur raincoat. 'Baby coat!'
Eshaan's face went red. He threw the raincoat on the floor and started to cry loudly, the kind of crying that makes everyone turn.
Chaitanya grabbed his hand. Their class teacher, Mr Pinto, crouched down. 'Eshaan, big feeling. Is it more hurt or more angry?'
'Hurt,' Eshaan hiccuped. 'And angry.'
'Both. Okay. Let's do our five balloon breaths by the window.'
They breathed together. Eshaan picked up the raincoat. 'I still like dinosaurs,' he said. Chaitanya said, 'Me too,' and meant it.

qa.q: What did the older boys laugh at?
qa.a: Eshaan's dinosaur raincoat.

qa.q: What was Eshaan feeling when he threw the raincoat on the floor?
qa.a: He felt hurt and angry at being teased, on top of disappointment about the cancelled relay.

qa.q: What choice did Mr Pinto make that helped Eshaan cool down?
qa.a: He crouched down, helped Eshaan name the feeling as hurt and angry, and led five balloon breaths by the window.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya feel watching Eshaan cry so loudly?
qa.a: Chaitanya may feel protective and caring, grabbing Eshaan's hand and standing by their shared love of dinosaurs.

grounding: Shows a child crushed by teasing into a loud upset, and an adult helping name the feelings and cool down.

passage: At the school in Shimla, Yusuf loved everything too much: he hugged his best friend so hard at the gate that they both fell over, and cried when the class hamster went home for the holidays. On Monday some boys laughed at his lisp during reading. Yusuf's face crumpled. He shouted, "I hate all of you!", knocked his chair over and sobbed under the table for a long time. Tenzin-sir didn't drag him out. He crouched and said, "You're really hurt and angry. That was mean of them." That afternoon he spoke to the boys, and then he and Yusuf made a cool-down card: three breaths, a drink of water, a squeeze of the stress ball. The next time teasing started, Yusuf pulled out the card first.

qa.q: What was on Yusuf's cool-down card?
qa.a: Three breaths, a drink of water, a squeeze of the stress ball.

qa.q: How did Yusuf feel when the boys laughed at his lisp?
qa.a: He felt crushed and hurt, then furious.

qa.q: What did Tenzin-sir do that helped?
qa.a: He named Yusuf's feelings, dealt with the teasing boys that afternoon and taught a cool-down plan.

qa.q: How might Yusuf's best friend see his big hugs?
qa.a: His best friend probably feels loved, even when the hug knocks them both over.

grounding: Shows a child who loves fiercely and is crushed by teasing, helped by an adult who names feelings and teaches cool-down steps.

passage:
Monday: Mridul's drawing of their dog won a sticker, and he danced round the kitchen, singing. Two hours later his brother Jeevan laughed at his wobbly cycling, and Mridul screamed, slammed the door and cried for an hour.
Wednesday: Jeevan said sorry. Papa sat with Mridul and helped him name it: "You felt embarrassed, then furious." They made a cool-down corner with a cushion and his comic books.
The next Sunday: At the park a boy called Mridul a baby. His fists clenched. He went quiet, walked to the bench and breathed. Then he came back, cheeks red, and said loudly, "That was mean." Afterwards he told Papa, "I was so angry, but I used the bench."

qa.q: What won a sticker?
qa.a: Mridul's drawing of their dog.

qa.q: What did Mridul feel when Jeevan laughed at his cycling?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed, then furious.

qa.q: How did Papa help Mridul turn big feelings into something manageable?
qa.a: He helped name the feelings and set up a cool-down corner, which Mridul later used as the park bench.

qa.q: How might Jeevan feel after Mridul's hour of crying?
qa.a: Jeevan likely feels sorry, which is why he apologised on Wednesday.

grounding: Shows over days a child with strong feelings learning to name them and cool down.

passage: Tushar, beta, you remind me of myself. At nine I loved my goat Moti so fiercely I slept in the shed. When the boys at school teased me about it, I cried so loudly the headmaster came out. I'd rage for hours, bang the door, refuse dinner. My father said, "Stop this drama." That only made it worse. But my mother would sit on the step and say, "Your heart is big, Akash. Big hearts feel big storms." She taught me to walk to the neem tree and count its branches until the storm got smaller. I, Akash, still feel everything strongly. But now I call it passion. It's why I became a vet.

qa.q: What was the goat's name?
qa.a: Moti.

qa.q: How did young Akash feel when the boys teased Akash about Moti?
qa.a: Akash felt crushed and furious, crying loudly and raging for hours.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story?
qa.a: The mother naming Akash's big heart and teaching a way to count the neem tree's branches until the storm passed.

qa.q: How did the father's "Stop this drama" affect young Akash?
qa.a: It made the upset worse, because the feelings were dismissed instead of understood.

grounding: Shows a child who loves fiercely and has long upsets, helped by a parent who names feelings and teaches a way to cool down.

passage:
Jahnavi loved her new puppy so much she made him a birthday card on his first week home. So when Rohit laughed at the card in class, saying only babies make cards for dogs, she ran out of the room.
It was the last day before the exams, the teacher was busy with revision, and the corridor was noisy with the cleaners. Jahnavi cried loudly by the water cooler.
Jaya Ma'am, the class teacher, found her there between periods. She had only five minutes. "You're hurt and embarrassed, right?" Jahnavi nodded, sobbing. "Let's cool the fire first. Breathe in like smelling a flower, out like blowing a candle." They did it four times.
"Your big love for that puppy is a good thing," Jaya Ma'am said. "We'll talk to Rohit after the bell." Jahnavi wiped her face and walked back in.

qa.q: Where did Jahnavi cry after running out of class?
qa.a: She cried loudly by the water cooler in the corridor.

qa.q: Why did Rohit's joke hit Jahnavi so hard?
qa.a: She loved her puppy fiercely, so the teasing made her feel deeply hurt and embarrassed, not just a little annoyed.

qa.q: What did Jaya Ma'am do that could help Jahnavi next time?
qa.a: She named the feelings and taught a quick breathing way to cool down, which Jahnavi can use herself even when adults are busy.

qa.q: If you were Rohit, what might change after the teacher talks to you?
qa.a: Rohit might realise the joke landed much harder than intended and see that Jahnavi's love for her puppy is not babyish.

grounding: Jahnavi's fierce love and crushing upset after teasing are met with named feelings and a cool-down skill, turning intensity toward passion.
